purpose: The two menus the top bar mounts — NotificationMenu (the bell) and ProfileMenu (the avatar, which also carries theme selection). Both are fds DropdownMenus.

useInstead.use: fds DropdownMenu directly — these two carry product behaviour, not just a panel

useInstead.when: the panel is a full page of notifications
useInstead.use: a route — the bell previews the top few and links onward

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for the iosense top-bar menus.
decision.beforeTheRules: Both are mounted by AppTopBar and sit at the right edge in a fixed order — bell, then avatar. Anything else the host adds goes to their left, so these two never move.

rules.if: you are adding a control near them
rules.because: it lands to their left and the two fixed positions hold

rules.then: pass the full list newest-first plus `unreadCount`
rules.because: the bell previews only the top few, so the count has to come from the source rather than from the previewed slice

rules.then: close the menu as part of the handler
rules.because: a menu left open over the page the reader just moved to is the commonest complaint about menus like these

rules.then: pass `preference` and `onPreferenceChange` and let ProfileMenu render the tiles
rules.because: the three choices are light, dark and system, and system is a real third option rather than the absence of a choice — a two-way toggle cannot express it

rules.if: you need the resolved theme for your own UI
rules.then: read it from useAppTheme, not from the preference
rules.because: 'system' is not a theme; it is an instruction to follow the OS, and only the hook knows what that currently resolves to

constraints: Sign out is the one destructive row in the profile menu and is the only one styled with negative intent.

fds Tooltip and Popover clone their child with `getReferenceProps({ ref, ...children.props })` — props land AFTER ref, so a child carrying its own ref silently overwrites the merged one and the tooltip never opens. Never put a ref on the direct child of either.

accessibility.keyboard: Both open on click, close on Escape and on outside click, and return focus to their trigger.
accessibility.aria: Triggers carry aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. The unread count is part of the bell's accessible name rather than a separate announcement, so it is not read twice.
accessibility.notes: The avatar's image is alt="" because the trigger's label already names the user.

composition.childrenContract: None. Both take data — notifications as an array, the profile as an object.
composition.notes: ProfileMenu owns the appearance modal and the theme tiles; there is no separate theme control to mount.

antiPatterns.dont: Deriving the unread count from the previewed slice
antiPatterns.why: the bell shows only the top few, so a derived count under-reports as soon as there are more

antiPatterns.dont: Leaving the menu open after a row navigates
antiPatterns.why: the panel then covers the page the reader just asked for

antiPatterns.dont: Reducing the theme choice to a light/dark toggle
antiPatterns.why: 'system' is a distinct instruction, not the absence of a preference, and a toggle cannot represent it

antiPatterns.dont: Putting a ref on the direct child of an fds Tooltip or Popover
antiPatterns.do: Address it another way — a data attribute, or a ref on a wrapper
antiPatterns.why: the clone spreads children.props after ref, so yours wins and the component silently never opens

examples.canonical:
<AppTopBar
  notifications={items}
  unreadCount={unread}
  onOpenNotifications={() => go('notifications')}
  profile={profile}
  preference={preference}
  onPreferenceChange={setPreference}
  …
/>

incorrect.why: counts only the preview; pass the real total
the ref on the direct child clobbers the merged one and the tooltip never opens — with no error

examples.storybook:
npm run storybook -> Top nav/Profile menu. Each story opens its panel on mount,
because a bell and an avatar shown closed tell you nothing about what they do.

  Open                      the header (avatar, name, org Badge) + Settings / Theme / Log Out
  OpenWithInitials          no avatar image, so the trigger and header fall back to initials
  OpenOnDarkTheme           the Theme row names the CURRENT theme in its trailing slot
  AppearancePicker          the modal the Theme row opens — a sibling of the menu, not a child
  NotificationsOpen         a five-item preview, kind / source / when, then View more
  NotificationsEmpty        an fds EmptyState, not a blank panel
  NotificationsOverflowing  nine items, five shown
  NotificationsManyUnread   the pill caps rather than stretching the bar
